title: bn254-pairing-inversion: tower-arithmetic 1024-adding Pollard rho with partitioned Nivasch stacks, output (P0,[x]Q0)

claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the one-trial algorithm in proof.md (1024-adding multiplicative walk in the Fp2/Fp6/Fp12 tower, salted multiplicative-hash index on one Montgomery word, Nivasch cycle detection partitioned into 256 stacks of at most 512 entries, hard cap T=ceil(1.15*sqrt(r*1024/1023)) steps, exact recovery and verification of x) returns P=P0 and Q=[x]Q0 with e(P,Q)=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.39 (model prediction 0.4825; 0.4224 if the effective walk size is 20% larger), using at most 2^128.297935 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) in every run and at most 2^26 bytes of peak storage. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding random-mapping heuristic, supported and limited as explained in proof.md; degeneracy is bounded exactly by 1/r. The uniform cap R_total = T*49152 + 2^40 instructions includes all one-target setup, fresh randomness, table construction, subgroup check, stack work, failures, recovery, verification and output, justified in machine.md. No prior acceptance, advice, amortization or production-scale execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check tower Fp12 products against the protected basis and count their Fp operations; run word-level CIOS with an instruction tally; check BN254 generator order, walk invariant and output point; run the exact walk/stack/cap control flow on small prime-order groups and report every outcome; evaluate the success model; recompute the score. Finite-scope evidence only, not a production success proof.
